_comment: Example config covering all four stacks. Copy to gates.config.json at your repo root and delete the projects you do not have. JSON has no comments, so notes live in _comment and description fields, which the runner reads and ignores.
_comment_baselineDir: Commit this directory. A baseline is a reviewed record of known debt, so it belongs in git where a growing one shows up in a diff.
_comment_timeout: 10 minutes. Any single gate that needs more than that is not a local gate, it is a CI job.
_comment_order: Gates run in the order they are listed. Put them cheapest first: format, lint, type-check, unit tests, build. The first failure you hit should be the one that took 2 seconds to find.

projects.name: backend
projects._comment_paths: --only-changed skips this whole project when git reports no change under backend/.

gates._comment: exit-code produces no failure keys, so it cannot be baselined. Formatting is all-or-nothing anyway: run the formatter and the gate goes green.
Swap to a keyed parser if you want ruff baselined. exit-code here assumes you start from a clean lint.

gates._comment_run: -rfE prints the short summary lines FAILED path::test and ERROR path::test. That is where the keys come from, and it needs no plugin. -p no:cacheprovider keeps .pytest_cache out of the tree.
gates._comment_env: SKIP_DB_BOOTSTRAP keeps the gate hermetic. A gate must not need a live database.

gates._comment: Keys are file plus rule id. Line and column are dropped on purpose, so moving code does not invent NEW failures.

THE HOLE WORTH CLOSING. Most tsconfig.json files exclude test files, so `tsc --noEmit` never checks them and a broken test helper type stays invisible. tsconfig.gates.json extends tsconfig.json and adds the test globs back into include. Point this gate at that file, not at the default one.

gates._comment_reportFile: vitest prints progress on the same stream as the report, so write the JSON to a file and read it back. Add .gates-vitest.json to .gitignore.

gates._comment: Last in the ladder because it is the slowest. A build failure the type-check did not catch is rare, but it is the one that breaks the deploy.

gates._comment_run: -json is required. The parser reads the event stream and keys failures as Package.TestName, subtests included.

projects._comment: Java service. Maven surefire writes JUnit XML, which is what the parser reads.
projects.name: billing-java

gates._comment_reportFile: A directory is walked for every .xml inside it. A single file path also works. Gradle writes to build/test-results/test.
